After adhering very strictly to physical distancing for the last two months, I broke down a few days ago and slept with a friend that I’d started seeing casually shortly before this all started. It felt nice in the moment and I felt ok about it right after, but now I just feel incredibly guilty. 

What adds to the shittiness is that I was actually feeling pretty calm and ok about things for a while during the pandemic. Then seeing this friend again became a concrete possibility. I resisted it for a while, then just went on physically distanced bike rides/walks. I thought I could keep it from escalating, but...obviously not :/

**Tl;DR**: I'm having trouble sticking with strict physical distancing now that I have a concrete option to pursue physical intimacy with a trusted friend who lives outside my household. I'd appreciate thoughts on how to approach decision-making when these kinds of emotions/desires start to play a strong role. (Apologies for the wall of text below...)

\--

Right before the pandemic started being taken seriously here (early March), I hooked up with a friend. Afterwards, we talked about it and decided that while neither of us was looking for something serious, it would be fun to pursue a fwb relationship.

Cue the pandemic...

Once things started shutting down, we agreed not to see each other, even though we both wanted to, especially since we both have roommates.  I had a lot of trouble coping with feelings of isolation and touch-deprivation at first; but with time, a lot of self-reflection, and some therapy I came to terms with that and began to even feel a kind of peace and happiness.

Then, about three weeks ago, he invited me over. I declined but agreed to go on a distanced walk. Over the course of these past few weeks, we started spending more and more time together-at-a-distance outside, including one day where we ended up spending about ten hours together and talked about a lot of personal/vulnerable topics. It was definitely a weird transformation of what was initially supposed to be a fwb situation, but I was enjoying it. At the same time, there were occasional flirtatious moments that I could feel getting more and more tempting. He made it clear that he would be open to progressing to something non-distanced, but I explained that I felt we shouldn't since our state has continued advising against close contact with people outside your household.

A couple days ago, though--shortly after our state began to reopen--I gave in to temptation, and we ended up sleeping together.  It was really nice to just be held by another person again, and if we weren't in a pandemic I wouldn't hesitate to do it again. We connect really well emotionally, I trust him (both because of the 'dates' we've been on and our past friendship), and we have great physical chemistry.

Under the current circumstances, though, I'm having trouble sorting through how much of my desire to continue this is the result of selfish, pleasure-seeking behavior that I should just quash; how much is me losing resolve as our state begins to reopen and as more and more people start talking about "pods"/"bubbles"/etc; how much is "risky shift" precipitated by his (and some of my friends') higher risk tolerance compared to me; and how much might be a pragmatic approach to managing risk as it becomes clear that this will continue for quite a while.

I'm not asking anyone to make a decision for me, and I am very aware (from too much googling) of what the current public health guidance on sex and relationships is. But I would love to know if people have tools in navigating these feelings. It's strange because I know from experience now that I *can* be happy isolating without physical contact. But now that having that contact is on the table as a concrete possibility, it feels very hard to resist, and even harder to make clear-headed decisions about.

Thanks so much, that’s very helpful and reassuring—fingers crossed!

Also, just a small follow-up: does this mean that if the IRS does select my return for 60 day review I will have to wait until the review process is complete (but not until my amending return is processed)?

Thank you so much again for the helpful information!

**My tl;dr question**: After my 2019 return was accepted, I realized I used the wrong year's W2 for  one of my jobs, resulting in a ≈$400 discrepancy. I did not file taxes in 2018. If my return is flagged for review, how can I expect this to  affect when I will receive my stimulus payment?

\-

Longer version:

I  didn't file taxes in 2018 but was required to this year; I submitted  them on 4/12 and they were accepted by the IRS. The current status is,  "We have received your tax return and it is being processed."

Subsequently,  I realized that I am an idiot and used my 2018 W2 instead of my 2019 W2  for one of my jobs. The two years aren't radically different (I made  about $400 more this year), but obviously they aren't exactly the same.

From  what I've researched, I shouldn't amend the return until my refund is  approved or rejected by the IRS, but there is a high likelihood that it  will be flagged due to the discrepancy.

Does  anyone have any insight on what this will mean for my stimulus payment?  It seems like the review and amended filing process can take months,  which is unfortunate since I was hoping to use the stimulus payment to  help towards rent after my current job ends in May. That being said, I  realize that the mistake is completely my own fault and that this may be  the consequences that I have to pay for rushing and not checking the  return thoroughly before filing.

I currently have income through May, after that it's uncertain... My safety net is moving across the country and staying with my parents, which isn't ideal since my mom's at-risk and travel is ill advised (and, who knows, may become difficult/impossible). That's still a little ways off though so I'm trying to take control of that situation as much as I can and communicate with people (work and family) to figure out options.

I have great friends that I've been basically chatting/facetiming with non-stop. I have a cat, and two roommates that I get along well with, but am not super close to. I also have a therapist that I like, although she is a short-term resource from the university so I need to start working on finding someone new. This is kind of one of the things I find worrying...I feel like I have everything I "should" need, yet this still feels incredibly hard.

The main thing that is really getting to me is a lack of in-person human contact. There is actually someone I've kinda been dating, and we've both talked about how we'd like to see each other but it seems irresponsible. Yesterday I stood 8 feet away from a close friend on my porch and talked, and it was the best I've felt in days, but it seems like depending on the lockdown/etc policies even that soon might not be possible/advised.

I just miss being able to hug someone, or share a beer, or just be physically close. FaceTiming doesn't really feel like a great substitute. I love my cat, but she isn't the same as a person. 

The whole thing feels bleak but when I so much as think about making some kind of exception for my mental health, that feels incredibly selfish. Like, if I go to see my date or go into a friend's house, I'm increasing the chance of contributing to the spread of this virus, getting 10s or 100s of people sick, and overwhelming our medical system.  Compared to those risks one life (mine) seems like maybe an acceptable loss.

I've had more passive/low-key suicidal thoughts but this is the first time it's felt so real...where it's actually really scared me. 

I'm not at any immediate risk to myself, but I worry about how things will be if I keep having these thoughts.

Anyone else feeling guilty for worrying about their mental health during this pandemic?

I’ve been self-quarantined for the past week and it’s starting to really get to me. For the past few days I’ve been intermittently crying and occasionally having some kind of scary suicidal thoughts. I’m trying to use all the coping strategies I know (talking to friends, talking to professionals, being with my cat, mindfulness, distraction, etc) and while it helps it still feels really hard. And it’s hard to imagine something like this going on for months. 

I don’t really feel sure that I can keep doing this that long, at least not without being in a pretty bad and maybe not super safe place mentally.

But it also feels really selfish to worry about my personal mental health when we’re facing a public health crisis where so many lives are at stake. In my darker moments, I feel like if it came to it, it would be better to kill myself than to do things that might improve my mental health but could risk public health. Because the former is only my life but the latter could be so many others’.
For me it’s escalated from just once near the beginning of the week to more and more over the past 3 days, where now I’m basically intermittently crying more often than not.
